questions.q: When multiple routing table entries could match a packet's destination, which one does a router choose?
options: The most specific match — a /32 beats a /24, which beats the default /0 route
Always the default route regardless of other matches
The oldest entry in the table
A random entry among the matches
questions.explain: Routers use longest-prefix (most specific) matching — a /32 host route beats a broader /24 subnet route, which beats the catch-all /0 default route.

questions.q: What is a device's default gateway?
options: The router it sends traffic to when the destination isn't on its own local subnet
The device's own IP address
The DNS server it uses
A backup device used only when the primary device fails
questions.explain: The default gateway is the router a device hands traffic to for any destination outside its own local subnet — it then relies on the gateway's own routing table.

questions.q: What's the key weakness of a static route compared to dynamic routing?
options: A static route doesn't automatically adapt if a link goes down — someone has to notice and fix it
Static routes can't be configured by administrators
Static routes only work on wireless networks
Static routes are always slower to use
questions.explain: A static route is manually configured and fixed — it won't adapt on its own if a link fails, unlike dynamic routing protocols that recalculate paths automatically.

questions.q: What is BGP (Border Gateway Protocol) used for?
options: Routing within a single office's local network only
Assigning IP addresses to new devices
Encrypting traffic between two routers
Exchanging routing information between separate autonomous systems — effectively holding the public internet's routing together
questions.explain: BGP is the exterior gateway protocol used between autonomous systems, most notably across the public internet, where major ISPs exchange routes with their neighbors.

questions.q: Why does traffic taking an unexpected network path matter to a SOC analyst, not just a network engineer?
options: Routing paths are always identical regardless of security posture
It never matters to security — routing is purely a performance concern
Only BGP-level routing has any security relevance
An unexpected route or a device reaching somewhere it has no legitimate reason to can be a real indicator worth investigating
questions.explain: Traffic following a route that shouldn't exist, or a device reaching a destination it has no business reaching, is a practical indicator a SOC analyst should recognize and investigate.
